candidates.title: filterDropdown does not manage tab (usability regression since 4.19)
candidates.reason: Named4.18.9/4.21.5 pair; parent36176 fix38585 stops Enter propagation but does not establish repair for this original Tab criterion.
candidates.issueBody:
### Reproduction link

[![Edit on CodeSandbox](https://codesandbox.io/static/img/play-codesandbox.svg)](https://codesandbox.io/s/antd-filterdropdown-focus-issue-yy73v8)

### Steps to reproduce

- Add `filterDropdown` option to a column
- Press on the filter icon
- Focus on an input element
- Press `tab`

### What is expected?

Focus moves to the next element

### What is actually happening?

Focus is lost and filter dropdown is closed

| Environment | Info |
| --- | --- |
| antd | 4.21.5 |
| React | 17.0.2, 18.0.0 |
| System | MacOS 12.4 (21F79) |
| Browser | Chrome |

---
[Here's a link to the last working version](https://codesandbox.io/s/antd-filterdropdown-focus-issue-last-working-version-9tp2mv) (4.18.9) - it is the same code, the only difference is the antd version. Please also note that the bug occurs with React 17 and 18, so it's not related to `render` vs `createRoot` mounting implementation.

candidates.title: Regression: overlaytrigger tooltip does not disappear when used with dropdown button
candidates.reason: Original criterion is pointer mouseleave/click tooltip dismissal; no original keyboard criterion.
candidates.issueBody:
See:
![overlaytrigger-bug](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/30173/9492248/ba5893fe-4baa-11e5-8bee-42fb8e956010.gif)

``` jsx
  <OverlayTrigger placement='top' overlay={<Tooltip>Hello World</Tooltip>}>
    <DropdownButton title="Menu">
      <MenuItem>Click Me</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem>Click Me</MenuItem>
    </DropdownButton>
  </OverlayTrigger>
```

Expected behavior:
Tooltip should disappear as soon as user moves mouse out of the button.

Actual behavior:
Tooltip does not disappear when user moves mouse from the button to the menu.
Tooltip does not disappear when user clicks on a menu item.
Tooltip does not disappear until after user moves mouse on to the trigger element and then back out to force mouseleave event.

Used to work correctly in the previous release.

candidates.title: [Tabs][composite] v1.7.0 regression: infinite render loop ("Maximum update depth exceeded") when a composite item's render child has an unstable ref (e.g. react-router NavLink)
candidates.reason: Both reports lead to same composite ref-loop fix5441; batch23 tests one compatible router-tab construct. Never count duplicates as separate patterns.
candidates.issueBody:
# Bug report

## Current behavior

Since **v1.7.0**, a `<Tabs.Tab>` rendered as a react-router `<NavLink>` (the standard router-tabs pattern) throws on **mount** — no interaction required:

> Error: Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component repeatedly calls setState inside componentWillUpdate or componentDidUpdate. React limits the number of nested updates to prevent infinite loops.

```tsx
<Tabs.Tab value="" nativeButton={false} render={<NavLink to="" end />}>One</Tabs.Tab>
```

The loop runs through the new synchronous map-update path in `CompositeList`:

```
dispatchSetState (react-dom)
  @base-ui/react/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.mjs:37     // setMapTick, in scheduleMapUpdate
  @base-ui/react/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.mjs:45     // unregister
  @base-ui/react/internals/composite/list/useCompositeListItem.mjs:45  // ref callback -> unregister(previousNode)
  @base-ui/utils/useMergedRefs.mjs:95                              // forkRef.cleanup
```

This worked on **v1.6.0** and broke on **v1.7.0** (the release that reworked CompositeList lifecycle timing).

## Expected behavior

The tab should render once and settle, as it did on v1.6.0. A composite item whose `render` child supplies an unstable (new-identity-per-render) callback ref should not cause the composite list to re-enter `register`/`unregister` indefinitely. Composing refs with a fresh callback each render is common (react-router `NavLink`, and many wrapper/link components, do it), so it should be tolerated.

## Reproducible example

**https://stackblitz.com/github/tomas-gerzicak/base-ui-1.7.0-tabs-loop-repro**
(source: https://github.com/tomas-gerzicak/base-ui-1.7.0-tabs-loop-repro)

Open it and check the console — it throws `Maximum update depth exceeded` on mount. The entire app:

```tsx
import { MemoryRouter, NavLink } from 'react-router';
import { Tabs } from '@base-ui/react/tabs';

function App() {
  return (
    <MemoryRouter>
      <Tabs.Root value="">
        <Tabs.List>
          <Tabs.Tab value="" nativeButton={false} render={<NavLink to="" end />}>One</Tabs.Tab>
          <Tabs.Tab value="two" nativeButton={false} render={<NavLink to="two" />}>Two</Tabs.Tab>
        </Tabs.List>
      </Tabs.Root>
    </MemoryRouter>
  );
}
```

## Base UI version

v1.7.0 (regression from v1.6.0). `@base-ui/utils` 0.3.2, react 19.2, react-router 7.18.1.

## Which browser are you using?

Reproduced in Chromium and in a React 19.2 + jsdom test environment (`@testing-library/react`). The loop is in Base UI's reconciliation (`CompositeList` → `useMergedRefs`), not environment-specific — "Maximum update depth exceeded" is React's runtime loop guard.

## Which OS are you using?

macOS (also fails on Ubuntu CI).

## Which assistive tech are you using (if applicable)?

N/A

## Additional context

I bisected the trigger down to ref stability of the `render` child:

- `render={<a href="#a" />}` (static element) — **no loop**
- `render` child that re-renders itself once (`useEffect` setState) — **no loop**
- `render` child with a **memoized** (`useCallback`) merged ref — **no loop**
- `render` child with an **unstable per-render callback ref** (what `NavLink` installs) — **loops**
- `<Tabs.Indicator>` is not required; `Tabs.Root` + `Tabs.List` + two tabs is enough.

Suspected root cause — interaction of two v1.7.0 changes:

1. `useCompositeListItem`'s ref is merged (via `useMergedRefs`) with the `render` child's ref. When the child supplies a new callback-ref identity each render, `useMergedRefs` returns a new merged callback each render, so React detaches the old ref (→ `unregister(previousNode)`) and attaches the new one (→ `register(node)`) on **every commit**.
2. `CompositeList`'s `scheduleMapUpdate` calls `setMapTick` **synchronously** on each `register`/`unregister` (the dep-less `useIsoLayoutEffect` that runs `flush()`), forcing another commit — which re-runs the merged ref — which unregisters/registers again → infinite loop.

A fix could skip the synchronous re-render when the same node re-registers (map contents unchanged), or make (un)registration resilient to a merged ref that detaches+reattaches the same DOM node within a commit.

candidates.issueBody:
# Bug report

## Current behavior

A `Tabs.Tab` whose `render` target is a `react-router` `Link` puts `CompositeList` into an unbounded update loop on 1.7.0. Rendering the tab list once is enough:

> Error: Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component repeatedly calls setState inside componentWillUpdate or componentDidUpdate. React limits the number of nested updates to prevent infinite loops.

```
❯ Object.<anonymous> node_modules/@base-ui/react/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.mjs:37:5
❯ Object.<anonymous> node_modules/@base-ui/react/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.mjs:45:5
❯ node_modules/@base-ui/react/internals/composite/list/useCompositeListItem.mjs:45:7
❯ Object.forkRef.cleanup node_modules/@base-ui/utils/useMergedRefs.mjs:95:24
```

```tsx
import { Tabs } from '@base-ui/react/tabs'
import { Link } from 'react-router'

function TabList() {
  return (
    <Tabs.List>
      <Tabs.Tab value="general" nativeButton={false} render={<Link to="/org" />}>
        General
      </Tabs.Tab>
    </Tabs.List>
  )
}
```

## Expected behavior

Renders once and settles, as on 1.6.0.

## What I narrowed it to

One `Tabs.Tab` with a `Link` is enough; the other tabs can be plain. Four variants, same test file, same 1.7.0 install:

| `render` target | Result |
|---|---|
| `<Link to="…" />` (react-router) | ✗ loops |
| `(props) => <Link {...props} to="…" />` (callback form) | ✗ loops |
| local component that renders `<Link>` | ✗ loops |
| `<a href="…" />` (intrinsic) | ✓ fine |
| local component that renders `<a>` | ✓ fine |

So it is not the `render` prop shape and not component-vs-intrinsic: it is `Link` itself. Wrapping it does not break the chain. On 1.6.0 every variant renders fine.

The trace bottoms out in `useMergedRefs`' `forkRef.cleanup` calling back into `useCompositeListItem`, which re-registers into `CompositeList` and setStates, so the suspects on my side are the 1.7.0 changes around ref/lifecycle timing: "Correct layout and passive effect timing" (#5337), "Remove redundant lifecycle synchronization" (#5341), "Prevent stale cleanup from clearing registered part IDs" (#5340), and in Composite "Fix nested list reorder detection" (#5156).

This looks like the same interaction as #3245 (`[tooltip] "Maximum update depth exceeded" when trigger is react-router Link`), which was a beta-5 regression fixed in 2025, resurfacing in the composite list path.

## Versions

- `@base-ui/react` 1.7.0 (1.6.0 is unaffected)
- `@base-ui/utils` 0.3.2
- `react` / `react-dom` 19.2.8
- `react-router` 8.3.0 (current latest)
- Reproduced under jsdom + Vitest, and in a Playwright run against a real browser where the page never finishes rendering.

This fix will be available in the next npm release of Base UI.

In the meantime, use the [canary build](https://base-ui.com/react/overview/releases#canary-releases) from [PR #5441](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/5441):

```sh
npm i https://pkg.pr.new/@base-ui/react@ba41f1f
```

This installs a complete package for `@base-ui/react` with the fix included. It is hosted by pkg.pr.new rather than npm, and the URL is available for up to six months.
